tools.name: evaluate_job
tools.description: Rate a job posting against Justin's criteria. Use when the posting has enough information to rate: company, role, location/remote status, and compensation.

tools.name: flag_for_review
tools.description: Flag a posting for manual review. Use when key information (compensation, remote status) is missing or ambiguous, so the job can't be rated reliably. If compensation is missing, try research_company first; flag only if research finds no pay.

tools.name: research_company
tools.description: Look up stored facts about a company: size, stage, and typical base pay for a role level. Use when a posting doesn't list compensation.

payload.job_text:
Tallowmere Robotics — AI Product Manager
Location: Remote (US)
Compensation: $140,000–$165,000 base

Tallowmere Robotics makes inspection robots for warehouses and distribution centers. We're adding AI features that let site managers ask questions about inspection results in plain language and get suggested maintenance actions.

As AI Product Manager, you'll own the natural-language assistant from prototype to launch. You'll work with our robotics and data teams to decide what the assistant can answer, how it explains its sources, and when it should hand off to a technician.

What you'll do:
- Define assistant use cases with site managers
- Prototype question-answering flows with LLM APIs
- Set accuracy targets and run evaluation before each release

What you bring:
- 5+ years in product management
- Hands-on experience with LLM APIs or search products
- Interest in industrial or hardware products

Fully remote in the US. Base salary $140,000–$165,000 plus equity.

content.text:
I rated this posting **IGNORE**.

- **Reason:** The base pay is $140K–$165K, and Justin's floor is $180K. The top of the range is still $15K under that.
- **Other details:** The role is fully remote in the US and includes equity. Equity wasn't enough to change the rating, because the floor applies to base pay.

The role itself is a reasonable fit. It's an AI PM job on an LLM-based assistant and asks for 5+ years of experience. The pay is the only problem.
